title: Why are we all so stressed?
reason: 本集从上一期的科技与 AI 轮换到工作生活平衡与压力管理，内容贴合工程交付、任务积压和管理责任等真实场景。所选表达以处理压力、说明后果和讨论应对方法为主，都是原文中可迁移的高频搭配，适合通过重复调用提升会议沟通和日常表达的流畅度。

targetExpressions.meaning: to cause someone to feel very worried, tense or under pressure
targetExpressions.usage: A last-minute production issue can make the whole team stressed out.

targetExpressions.meaning: to deal successfully with a difficult situation or feeling
targetExpressions.usage: A clear plan can help the team cope with a busy release week.

targetExpressions.meaning: to pause and breathe, often to become calmer before acting
targetExpressions.usage: Before replying to a difficult message, take a breath and think.

targetExpressions.meaning: to cause long-term physical or mental exhaustion from too much pressure or work
targetExpressions.usage: Constant overtime can lead to burnout if there is no time to recover.

targetExpressions.meaning: to make the greatest effort you reasonably can
targetExpressions.usage: Prepare carefully, then focus on doing your best in the presentation.

targetExpressions.meaning: designed as one solution for everyone, without considering different needs
targetExpressions.usage: There is no one-size-fits-all way to manage a software project.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Neil's idea using the target expression: Not having enough time can ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says that not having enough time to do something makes him stressed out.
In the episode, “cope with” means dealing with stressful situations or difficult feelings.

options.text: Neil pauses and breathes to cope with stress.
Neil copes stress with a pause.
Neil copes to stress by breathing.
Neil makes cope with the stress.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Neil's calming sequence: slow down, pause, ______ and think.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says he slows down, pauses and takes a breath when a situation feels stressful.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the cause-and-effect idea: If overwhelm becomes chronic stress, it may ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Claudia explains that long-term or chronic stress may eventually cause burnout.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: According to the episode, how can nerves sometimes help before an exam or performance?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Claudia says nerves can sharpen thinking and allow a person to do their best.

options.text: They can help you think clearly and do your best.
They always stop you from remembering anything.
They remove the need to prepare.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does “one-size-fits-all” mean in the discussion about stress?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme says different people may need different ways to manage stress; one solution does not suit every problem.

options.text: One method is applied to everyone, despite different needs.
Every person creates a completely new problem.
Only physical exercise can reduce stress.
A solution becomes more expensive for large groups.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence best reflects the episode's view of nerves?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript says nerves are not necessarily bad because they can sharpen the mind and support performance.

options.text: Nerves can sometimes help you focus and do your best.
Nerves always lead to burnout immediately.
Nerves mean you should avoid every difficult task.
Nerves and clear thinking can never happen together.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the workplace sentence: There is no ______ solution for helping every team member manage pressure.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: “One-size-fits-all” is the correct compound expression for a single solution that ignores individual differences.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80-120 words. Use this structure: (1) topic—why modern life can feel stressful; (2) two key ideas—when stress becomes harmful and how some stress may help; (3) practical conclusion about managing tasks or pressure. Phrase bank: “cope with”, “lead to burnout”, “one-size-fits-all”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate English is enough; rare vocabulary and complex sentences are not required.
referencePoints: Work, exams, world events and not having enough time are presented as sources of modern stress.
Neil slows down, pauses and takes a breath; Becca reminds herself that practice will help.
Temporary overwhelm can become chronic stress and may eventually lead to burnout.
Nerves are not necessarily harmful and can sharpen or concentrate the mind before a performance.
Stress-management methods are not one-size-fits-all, and accepting 'good enough' can reduce perfectionism.
A to-do list never truly ends because new tasks appear, so completing everything should not be the only measure of success.
